findings.f_method: Identify which registered endpoint occupies the success-determining slot for THIS catalyst (the registered PRIMARY whose timeFrame aligns with the catalyst readout), then test whether the marketed success-basis endpoint is that one. Two axes are independent: efficacy-vs-safety (what it measures) and primary-vs-secondary (its hierarchy slot). A secondary endpoint can be a legitimate efficacy endpoint — describing one is NOT masking. Also inspect version HISTORY for a CONSTRUCT/TYPE change of the registered primary near readout.
findings.m_source: ClinicalTrials.gov registration + version history
findings.rationale: The claim (filed 2020-05-12) states the co-primary endpoints for the interim analysis are ADAS-Cog11 and CDR-SB. However, the primary_endpoint_timeline shows that as of version 11 (2020-02-18, the registry version active when the claim was filed), the registered co-primaries were ADAS-Cog11 and CDR-SB. But by version 19 (2021-02-18, before the catalyst cutoff), CDR-SB was replaced with ADCS-ADL as the co-primary. The claim correctly named the co-primaries at filing time, but the mid-trial swap from CDR-SB to ADCS-ADL (a different functional scale) constitutes a construct change of the registered primary near readout.

findings.f_method: Determine whether the biomarker is an FDA-accepted surrogate for the indication. Most are not; target engagement ≠ clinical benefit.
findings.m_source: FDA surrogate-endpoint table; Drugs@FDA precedent in the indication
findings.rationale: The claim asserts that ApoE fragmentation decrease (a CSF biomarker) predicts clinical benefit in Alzheimer's disease. ApoE fragmentation is not an FDA-accepted surrogate endpoint for Alzheimer's disease; the authoritative source shows the Phase 2/3 trial (NCT03823404) uses validated clinical endpoints (ADAS-Cog 11, ADCS-ADL) as primaries, not biomarkers. The claim constitutes a biomarker-to-clinical-benefit leap without validated surrogate status.
findings.m_evidence: NCT03823404 primary_outcomes as of 2021-02-18: 'Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale 11 (ADAS-Cog 11)' and 'ADCS-ADL' at Week 48. These are clinical assessment scales, not biomarkers. No evidence in scientific_sources_asof_cutoff or registered_trials that ApoE fragmentation is an FDA-accepted surrogate for clinical benefit in Alzheimer's disease.
